reason: Changing window_size_s/stride_s/n_sample changes segment boundaries, so every grid point requires re-running frames->windows->embed for a representative sequence subset -- there is no way to compute this from embeddings already on disk (those are all for the current, single window config). This repo's own prior measurements put a single real ingest pass (19 sequences, current window config) at multiple minutes of CPU decode+detect+embed time even with the cheap X-CLIP path (docs/operations/STATUS.md Faz 1: 'frames 23.4 sn, YOLO 59.9 sn, X-CLIP 158.2 sn'); a multi-point grid (this module's default is 4 points) multiplies that. Given this session's remaining scope (Phase 2-11 of the implementation task are still pending), running even a minimal real sweep was not attempted -- doing so honestly requires a dedicated, budgeted session, not a fit-it-in pass.
required_command: Override config.yaml's window/merge/models.n_sample block per WindowConfig from bench.windowing_ablation.build_sweep(), then run `make frames && make windows && make detect && make embed MODEL=xclip_hf_zeroshot && make load MODEL=xclip_hf_zeroshot && make groundtruth && make eval` per config against the existing 19-sequence bench subset (config.yaml: bench.subset), feeding eval output into bench.windowing_ablation.run_screening(). Confirmation: repeat only the top 2-3 configs with MODEL=qwen3vl_emb_2048 (GPU strongly recommended given the 17.7-hour CPU cost this repo already measured for a single full Qwen ingest pass at the current window config -- docs/operations/STATUS.md Faz 4).
expected_environment: CPU is sufficient for X-CLIP/SigLIP2 screening (this environment could technically run it); Qwen confirmation needs a real GPU to stay inside a reasonable time budget.
